question:
A 66-year-old woman visits her primary care physician with a 1-month history of constipation and
intermittent flank pain that radiates to the groin. She also reports feeling weak throughout the day and
has been experiencing low mood for several months, attributing these symptoms initially to aging. Her
medical history includes hypertension and diabetes, for which she takes metformin and lisinopril. She
recently started taking a vitamin supplement. She consumes 2-3 alcoholic drinks on weekends and has
no history of smoking. Laboratory findings are as follows: Serum: Na+: 138 mEq/L Cl-: 104 mEq/L K+:
4.0 mEq/L HCO3-: 24 mEq/L BUN: 16 mg/dL Glucose: 138 mg/dL Creatinine: 1.2 mg/dL Ca2+: 11.8
mg/dL PO4-: 2.4 mg/dL What is the most likely cause of this patient’s symptoms? Answer Choices: (A)
Paraneoplastic syndrome (B) Thiazide diuretic use (C) Familial hypocalciuric hypercalcemia (D)
Multiple myeloma (E) Tertiary hyperparathyroidism (F) Metastatic bone disease (G) Glandular
adenoma (H) Ingestion of supplement (I) Sarcoidosis (J) Vitamin D intoxication
 A. Metastatic bone disease

B. Familial hypocalciuric hypercalcemia
C. Tertiary hyperparathyroidism
D. Paraneoplastic syndrome
E. Sarcoidosis
F. Thiazide diuretic use
G. Ingestion of supplement
H. Glandular adenoma
I. Vitamin D intoxication
J. Multiple myeloma
